title: El Quijote private transport operators protest fare and parking rules
location: El Quijote transport rank opposite Vladimir Ilich Lenin hospital, Holguín
organizer: Private truckdrivers, motorcycle operators and coachdrivers at El Quijote
participants_original: Ramón Zamora: about 10 motorcyclists, more than 25 coachdrivers, plus an unnumbered truckdriver fleet.
threshold_50_evidence: No total of simultaneous participants is reported. Approximate component estimates and an unnumbered fleet do not establish at least 50.

dates.summary: A January 6 report says Monday protest and Tuesday return to work, corresponding to January 4–5. End describes work resumption.

location_organizer.summary: Private transport operators demonstrated together at the named public rank.

demands.summary: Better income, ending parking charges and inspector harassment; the provincial transport director attended.

participants.summary: Component estimates and a fleet description leave total attendance unresolved.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Director René Rodríguez Morales met operators at the site and agreed fare and parking changes. Actual reception and agreement.

protester_violence.summary: The account says the situation nearly became violent. Actual violence is not established.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: Government fare and parking caps and inspectors were targeted. The protest was on the Monday before the January 6 report; operators returned to work Tuesday. A fleet is not a person count, and near violence does not establish actual violence.
open_questions: Verify total simultaneous demonstrators and whether another assembly followed the return to work.

title: Holguín siblings' reported peaceful protest before detention
location: Holguín province; precise protest site unknown
participants_original: Three named detainees; total protesters not reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Three named detainees are not a count of a qualifying public gathering.

start_date.summary: January reporting establishes only the month. January 6–7 detention chronology conflicts with January 7 incident labels.

location.summary: Holguín province and Gibara authorities are mentioned; the public protest site is unknown.

participants.summary: Three siblings are named; no crowd count.

demands.summary: The specific demand is unknown. Political affiliation alone does not establish it.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: The FDP's January 7 incident entries describe detention in reprisal for a peaceful protest. DDC relays a Directorio account of custody January 6–7. The physical protest date, public location and specific state-directed demand remain unverified; detention dates are not used as the start.
open_questions: Recover original protest account, physical date, public location, specific demand and crowd count; reconcile January 6 and 7.

title: UNPACU activists publicly challenge blocked food access
location: Public road beside UNPACU headquarters, Santiago de Cuba
threshold_50_evidence: Several activists does not establish at least 50.

dates_location.summary: Incident 28 explicitly identifies January 14, Santiago de Cuba and a public road.

demands.summary: Activists sought passage for a blocked meal recipient through a state-police cordon.

participants_protester_violence.summary: The FDP explicitly describes several activists protesting peacefully; organizational allegation.

state_response.summary: Passage was restored, but no formal reception or negotiation is documented. Prior cordon is not proof of a new response.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: The FDP says activists protested on the public road when police blocked Talía Álvarez and her daughter from reaching the headquarters meal service. They were allowed through. The police cordon predated January; this candidate concerns the reported new public action.
open_questions: Establish attendance and independent evidence; resolve relationship with January 15 under the missing Coding Procedure.

title: UNPACU headquarters protest over blocked Niubis Bisset
location: UNPACU headquarters, Santiago de Cuba; road versus inside premises uncertain
participants_original: Activists at headquarters; no number reported.
threshold_50_evidence: No evidence of at least 50; public character is also unresolved.

dates_location.summary: Incident 32 identifies January 15 and the headquarters, but not the exact protest space.

participants_protester_violence.summary: Peaceful protest is stated; no attendance count.

demands.summary: Police were blocking entry to the headquarters food service.

state_response.arrests.summary: Bisset was reportedly arrested on leaving after protesters helped her gain entry. Attribution to the protest rather than the wider cordon remains open.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: The FDP says activists at headquarters protested after Niubis Bisset was barred from entering. She gained entry, then was arrested on departure. The exact protest space may have been private premises. Relationship to the January 14 road action remains pending.
open_questions: Establish public space and attendance; resolve the episode boundary and whether Bisset's arrest responded to the protest.

title: Jobabo charcoal workers' reported wage protest
location: Jobabo municipality, Las Tunas; exact gathering unknown
organizer: Charcoal workers of Empresa Integral Agropecuaria de Las Tunas
participants_original: Unnumbered workers in Jobabo. The 22-person count describes a different site.
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance estimate for Jobabo; no transfer or summation of other sites.

dates_location.summary: The January 19 interview states that a protest also existed in Jobabo; no first day.

demands.summary: State-company wages and unpaid export bonuses were challenged. State-policy target requires review beyond ownership.

participants.summary: Unnumbered Jobabo workers are separate from 22 at another site.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: The January 19 Martí interview reports workers in Jobabo also protesting state-company wages and unpaid export bonuses. Public assembly, a local start day and coordination between sites remain unverified. State ownership alone does not establish the required policy target.
open_questions: Verify a public gathering, at least 50, local dates, state-policy target and any coordination with other sites.

title: Flight-ticket buyers repeatedly demonstrate at IACC
location: Outside IACC offices at 23 and P, El Vedado, Havana
participants_original: Numerous group on January 15; dozens on January 20. Thousands of ticket buyers describe the affected population.
threshold_50_evidence: Numerous or dozens without a total does not establish at least 50 at one gathering.

dates.summary: January 15 says gatherings already occurred that week. January 20 recalls Friday and Monday; January 21 says repeated visits. Exact first day and closure unknown.

location_demands.summary: Protesters outside IACC at 23 and P sought flight authorization and information from the Cuban regulator.

participants.summary: Dozens or numerous actual gatherers; thousands refers to the affected population.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The source describes an actual meeting in a room with the IACC president, national transport vice-minister and international-transport official. Demands remained unresolved.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police followed a threatened move to the Plaza de la Revolución. Actual dispersal is not established.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: Assemblies occurred by the week of January 11–15, with further visits January 18 and 20. The first day is unknown. Protesters demanded IACC authorization for Nicaragua flight frequencies, information and refunds. The Cuban regulator was targeted despite the initial allegation of private-agency fraud. Repeated visits remain one provisional episode.
open_questions: Establish at least 50, first physical date, repeated-visit episode boundary and the specific meeting date.

title: La Palma activists in pioneer costumes protest economic hardship
location: Street corner in La Palma, Havana
organizer: Osmel Adrián Rubio, Anyell Valdés Cruz, Jorge Luis Arias
participants_original: Three named activists; an unspecified multitude followed the police cars.
threshold_50_evidence: Three named protesters are below 50; the following crowd's participation and size are unresolved.

dates_location_organizer.summary: The body identifies January 22, a La Palma street corner and three named actors.

demands.summary: Slogans demanded food and milk, democracy and freedom.

participants.summary: Three actors plus an unnumbered crowd following arrest; participation by that crowd unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: All three were reportedly detained by police and State Security.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police placed the protesters in patrol cars and removed them from the corner, ending this physical action.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: Three activists demanded food and milk for children, democracy and freedom. ADN Cuba describes police removal with a crowd following. The following crowd's role and number are unknown, so it cannot be added automatically to the three demonstrators.
open_questions: Determine whether the following crowd joined the demonstration and whether at least 50 attended; obtain independent account.

threshold_50_evidence: No total or other clear evidence of at least 50.

demands.summary: State housing relocation, water, sanitation, food and prices; taxonomy unresolved.

participants.summary: Residents and families without a count or clear threshold evidence.

unknown_fields.summary: Unreported end dates, response categories, violence and other unknowns remain unknown. Silence does not establish absence.

notes: The January CCDDHH report describes shelter residents protesting housing, food prices and poor conditions in Bahía. It gives no precise date, original source, total or exact public space. Monthly placement remains tentative pending the original account.
